cards.title: The tumour tissue
cards.asks: How strongly must gap junctions couple cells for healthy tissue to turn a tumor back to the healthy state?

standing.says: Development work, not judged (D138). The record states none of this map's levels for it. Cells' own runs of the model of a public preprint made with BITSEY: J. Grodstein, J. Mathews and M. Levin, "Membrane voltage and connexin expression work together to enhance tumor growth and metastasis in cancer", bioRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.09.02.748840, version 1, 3 September 2026, CC-BY 4.0. It asks how strongly gap junctions must couple cells for healthy tissue to turn a tumour back to the healthy state. The user gave the work the highest priority on 17 November 2026 (D207), and its driver and its note are on main since that evening. Its linear model runs as written on the engine's own pieces, the reactions operator with the passive routes' neutral law on junction routes, unqualified, and its error against dense solves falls at second order; its exact Norton-equivalent network on the tissue model's own routes is its check. The preprint's tissue tables need engine features not built yet: a charged microRNA on junctions, a two-state junction gate and larger field solves (FR-15 to FR-17). On a line of 25 cells, the first six a tumour, the driver searched for the coupling at which the tumour returns to the healthy state; an engine check first stopped that search (FR-19), and after its fix the search ran again from main, followed by a ladder of ten couplings and a 9 by 9 sheet, an extension beyond the preprint's setup. On 18 November 2026 the user answered the note's questions (D219). Its next bundle, for a free seat: the correctly specified 25 by 25 threshold case, the preprint's Figure 5a through the windowed execution and record path, and BITSEY run unmodified, out of process, for pinned reference outputs, after its licence and revision are checked; the 2D search's registration states its geometry, success criterion, horizon, bracket, refinement rule and compute budget before it runs. Two judged comparisons were approved, each under a registered protocol with code-blind references: the linear model's numerical qualification, Figure 8 judged against independently derived physical balances, with the printed recursion's discrepancy kept as a finding; and the threshold comparison, whose verdict includes successful refinement and a convergence condition declared in advance, and in which only the 2D field is a true pre-registration, since the 1D line's value was already seen. For Table 3, its logged inputs and the interventions as actually executed govern the code's target, and the printed table is kept as a separate publication target, with the mapping discrepancies reported. FR-15 to FR-17 were scheduled with the owners whose files they touch, not yet started. The same evening the user put the core and the feature requests first (D222): the bundle's steps 2 to 5 and the references for the two judged comparisons wait for free seats and lanes. On 19 November 2026 charged species in the species operators, which the work's microRNA needs, were scheduled into the core pass as a general feature, starting with a diagnosis (FR-15's F2 part; D226, D228 item 4). By 20 November 2026 its first two steps had landed as general features: charged species in the reactions operator, where every reaction conserves charge, and a charged constant-field route law on the passive routes, on membranes first; hosting it on junctions waits for two answers from the tissue model's owner. Five quick worlds of this work form a set of crossrev, recorded from the engine's source before any core change, which every later core landing must regenerate bit for bit; that holds the engine to its own earlier programs, and compares nothing with the preprint. None of this is judged.

cards.title: FR-1: a closed compartment
cards.asks: Can a cell hold a closed compartment of its own, with its own volume and amounts, that exchanges species with the cell?

standing.says: A closed compartment inside a cell: a finite node the cell owns, bounded by one patch of its membrane, with its own volume and its own rows of the shared inventory. The user's high priority (14 November 2026). Its design is accepted (D169, 14 November 2026). Its first milestone, the declaration of a compartment, landed on 15 November 2026 as an operator. Since the rework landed on 16 November 2026, the operator admits the kinds of piece the engine knows on the compartment's bounding membrane, such as the proton pump and the proton leak, only under the implicit–explicit step whose checks hold their rates, and refuses any other kind. Since the evening of the same day it also admits FR-5's damage and pH condition, and a compartment whose admitted routes charge it can resume from its own checkpoint, in those worlds only (refusal 4 version 1.2, refusal 5 version 1.1). Its protocol, fr1-closed-compartment-v1, was registered and judged on 18 November 2026: it passed all 44 judged criteria against independent references written without the engine's code, and it is the exchange operator's first judged acceptance. Numerically qualified, on CPU only, within its scope line: the neutral first version as built at 05a8d193, with the exchange, turnover and reactions operators, no ion route and a zero anchor on the compartment, under the implicit–explicit step (ARS) at 1 ms and RK4 at 0.1 ms. The later doors, a compartment's creation, division, fission and fusion, and retirement, come with seam B of the core pass and the mitochondria work (D216). On 18 and 19 November 2026, after its judged runs, refusal 4 version 1.3 landed, which checks each move of a declared kind at the compartment's node against the step terms its law declares, and refusal 5 version 1.2, which admits a charge anchor where an admitted operator's routes charge the compartment, for FR-2; and membrane state now composes beside a compartment, but only together with FR-2's retrieval and recycling. Nothing was judged again, and the scope lines are unchanged.

cards.title: FR-4: compartment pH
cards.asks: Can a pump acidify a compartment against its gradient, with its protons buffered?

standing.says: Protons as a species, a pump that acidifies a compartment against its gradient, and buffering (feature request FR-4), one of the two priority users of the modular rework (D176). Protons are one species whose free part is set by a fast buffer rule at every stage, the proton pump is a transporter on the compartment's membrane, counterions are explicit, and its first case runs on fuel held constant. Its pump, its buffer and a proton leak landed on main with the rework on 16 November 2026, as pieces of the tissue model, together with the drivers that build its first world and the tools for its qualification. In a development run of that world, which is not a verdict, the compartment's pH stays within 1.4e-12 of the independent reference at a step of 1 ms, the energy accounts converge at second order as the step shrinks, and the planted errors are caught. Its independent references, written by a separate agent that read no engine code, show the compartment acidifying from pH 7.2 to about 5.1 against its gradient while the cytoplasm stays within 0.02 pH; without the counterion route it stalls. A kernel for treating the compartment's membrane implicitly in the step is on main too, with its tests; no model uses it yet, and chloride and pores wait for it. Its protocol, fr4-acidification-v1, was registered on 17 November 2026, after its rehearsal passed 21 of 21 criteria, and judged once the same day: it passed all 21 judged criteria against the independent references. Numerically qualified, on CPU only, within its scope line: the compartment operator as built at the registration commit, 32a1d439, with refusal 4 version 1.2 and refusal 5 version 1.1.

cards.title: FR-5: transfer across an internal membrane
cards.asks: Can a compartment's membrane leak and reseal, with transfer across it at a rate set by the compartment's own state, such as its pH?

standing.says: A compartment's membrane that can leak and reseal, with transfer across it at a rate that reads the compartment's own state, such as its pH (feature request FR-5), the other priority user of the modular rework (D176). It is built and on main since the evening of 16 November 2026, for development. Two kinds of piece, the damage of the compartment's membrane and a pH condition, act on the compartment's passive routes as factors, through a routing door the core built for any kind, and a compartment that holds charge can now resume from its own checkpoint, so FR-5's world starts from FR-4's steady state. In development runs, which are not verdicts, its declared world and its development world gave the same results bit for bit over 400 s on both of its arms, 800,000 steps each, including the burst of release after damage. Its independent references show the transfer slowing about 14-fold while the compartment is not acid enough, the leak releasing most of the compartment's cargo after damage, and the compartment acid enough again after about 330 s and 370 s. Its study of the time step passed its development reading late on 16 November 2026: every criterion holds on both arms, so the declared step of 0.5 ms stands. Its protocol, fr5-transfer-v1, was registered on 17 November 2026, after its rehearsal passed 51 of 51 criteria, and judged once the same day: it passed all 51 judged criteria against the independent references. Numerically qualified, on CPU only, within its scope line: the compartment operator as built at the registration commit, 32a1d439, with refusal 4 version 1.2 and refusal 5 version 1.1.

cards.title: FR-6: a species sets a channel's availability
cards.asks: Can the amount of a species set how available a channel population is, so that chemistry changes electrical behaviour?

standing.says: The rule by which a species amount in the inventory sets how available a junction or a channel population is, so chemistry can change electrical behaviour. It is in the engine since 14 November 2026: the Hill factors, the operator that applies them to junctions and to channels, and a slower two-state regulatory state. The operator was numerically qualified on 15 November 2026, on CPU and within its stated scope. It also answers feature request FR-6, species-driven control factors. FR-6's first item, the channel target, is qualified for channel populations without gates by that judged run, and on 18 November 2026 a second judged protocol, A5″, passed all 18 of its judged criteria: two cells' potassium leak populations driven through the slower regulatory state from different starting states, under the same dose. Numerically qualified within its scope line: the operator with its regulatory state and the secreted-species turnover as built at 555d8771, two pump-free 2 pL cells over 2 s, synthetic values, CPU only; gated channels, the routing door, leak and pump targets and any biological comparison are not covered. FR-7's design note, proposed on 18 November 2026 with options and the user's questions, frames the user's choice of the closed loop's unit; the coupling operator's rate route that it needs became a step of its own in the core pass, to go ahead only if the user's answer on the hold of D145 admitted a loop from species to control to production (D216, amended). The user answered that evening (D217, D218): the first loop is a membrane channel population, the junction channel next; its first acceptance is numerical, on synthetic lifetimes labelled so; the closed loop is not called qualified until a closed feedback case passes beside a control in which the feedback is cut; and physical production feedback is admitted through the one routing door, each loop verified whole. Its core prerequisites, B1's lifecycle driven by roles and the kinds' declarations, landed on 19 November 2026, and the loop's pieces followed on 19 and 20 November 2026: the coupling operator's version 2, with the rate route and a population's abundance as a source, and a unit producer. FR-7's first closed loop was judged on 20 November 2026 and passed (a part of its own, Abundance to function (FR-7)); that verdict is FR-7's, in its own scope, and adds nothing to this part's scope line.

cards.title: FR-7: abundance to function, in a closed loop
cards.asks: Can a transient template change a protein's abundance, and so a measurable response, in a loop that feeds back on itself?

standing.says: Judged in one scope only: FR-7's first closed loop, its comparison F4 against the code-blind reference R-loop, passed on 20 November 2026; F3's six-world comparison against its own references is queued, and every piece of the loop is development, not judged, on its own part. The request: the amount of a protein in the composite sets how a membrane population conducts, and a declared species can drive the rate at which it is made, so that a transient template changes a measurable response that may or may not outlive it (feature request FR-7). The user's answers of 18 November 2026 set the first loop's unit, admitted the loop through the one routing door, and ruled that a closed loop is not called qualified until a closed feedback case passes beside a control in which the feedback is cut (D217, D218). Its pieces landed on 19 and 20 November 2026: the unit producer, whose removal of units inside itself is a scoped exception to D177 that the user accepted (D232); the coupling operator's version 2, with a factor on another operator's rate and a population's abundance as a source; the producer's assembly rate as a target (F3); declared initial units per maturation pool; and the comparison code, the mappers and comparisons of the chain and of the loop, which has no test of its own. For the closed loop, under the user's delegation, the Na/K pump with Na-leak units at a declared synthetic time scale was chosen (D231), and its world scales the template's half-saturation and dose five-fold (D233). Its world, as its mapper declares it: one cell of the composite over the tissue model @3, with the Na/K pump on held fuel, membrane state's K-leak and Na-leak populations, species turnover, the coupling operator's version 2 and the unit producer. The judged run, from a frozen snapshot of main with the registered interface, ran both arms, closed and clamped: every compared row is within its band, the cut's applied factor is within its registered bound, the clearance row equals the registered 260 s, all 30 persistence rows pass, and the pump's rate read from the engine's own readouts matches its cumulative ledger. Its values are synthetic and labelled so.

cards.title: The composite on the L4
cards.asks: Does the composite model give the same answers on the L4 GPU as on the CPU, within a registered tolerance?

standing.says: Does the composite model give the same answers on the L4 GPU as on the CPU, within a registered tolerance? On the judged run, W1 and W2 pass and G2-Q1 passes Q1 to Q6. Q7, which asks for bitwise equality, failed on that run because of the L4's own nondeterminism at 825 nodes, and that verdict stands, since the protocol judges once. cards.title: Planarian loop

standing.says: The first living-cell loop, on main since the evening of 16 November 2026 with the run-view writer: a builder for the planarian's loop and one driver for every package. cards.title: Origin-of-life laws (OL1)
cards.asks: Do the origin-of-life engine's first laws hold against references written without the engine's code?

standing.says: Landed for development, not judged (18 November 2026). The four laws of the origin-of-life engine's first milestone (OL1), physical chemistry in an assembly: mass action for a step's encounter, in exact molecule counts (cells.stochastic_mass_action@1); catalysis as a factor on the state a step and its reverse share, so that a catalyst speeds or slows both alike and never moves an equilibrium (cells.transition_state_factor@1); and two terms of one free energy of the counts, ideal mixing, exact in the counts, and the membrane's regular mixing (cells.ideal_mixing@1, cells.regular_mixing@1). Each step comes as a forward and reverse pair, the reverse rate from the exact change of that free energy, so every pair keeps local detailed balance. Each law is declared on the family's own interfaces of seam F's template, with the works it cites, and the engine's declarations list all four. They follow the lead's rulings written into the design note. Against OL5's references, registered before any engine output, they passed 6 of 6 rows on 18 November 2026. Nothing is judged under a registered protocol, and nothing is compared with experiment. Implemented and guarded: on main with their tests, among them the laws' registration and the kernel's detailed balance, in tiers 1 and 2 of the engine's test tiers.

cards.title: FR-2: membrane retrieval and recycling
cards.asks: Can membrane move from a cell's surface into a pool inside the cell and back, with its charge following it?

standing.says: Development, not judged. Membrane moves between a cell's plasma membrane and a receiving pool inside the cell, a compartment the cell owns, and back, with the charges following the membrane: version 1 of feature request FR-2, on main since 19 November 2026 (D217). The retrieved membrane keeps its charge, no fluid moves, the pool is one well-mixed compartment per cell, channel units taken in are silent and held in the operator's record until they return, and no fuel is drawn for the machinery, so the version claims no total energy of trafficking. The charge, heat and work of every move are booked, and the energy ledger closes. Its registered comparison against independent references written without its code ran twice on 19 November 2026: the first run passed 770 of its 782 rows; after a blind correction of the references' floor for one class of checks, the second passed all 782, which is weaker evidence after the failed first run. The comparison is on main and checks every row in every gate. The third external review's fix of the same day refuses two routes of one cell. Implemented and guarded: tests on main check its laws, its runs on batches and sheets, and every row of the comparison.

cards.title: FR-8 rung 0: order through a switch
cards.asks: Why does the fine engine's order of accuracy drop when a cue switches a cell for good?

standing.says: Development, not judged. The measurements and the harness that come before a long-duration mode is chosen (feature request FR-8), all on today's fine engine. Stage 0 landed on main on 19 November 2026: five measurements, each with its criteria registered before its run, and the harness, a world of an hour whose cue at its midpoint switches a cell for good, run at three steps. Stage 0 makes no qualification claim, since its references are the engine's own runs. A ladder of rungs was then decided, with the user's agreement (D224): rung 0 first, to explain why the fine engine's order of accuracy drops through a switch, before any later rung is registered, and every later accuracy study judged against it. Rung 0 ran the same day, on the tissue model alone. Its registered verdict is "instrument not validated": its control for the slow phase had no power, so no cause is identified. Under an amendment registered blind before the main windows were read, the weaker evidence, the instruments pass and the cause is the transient before the step's order settles: the observed orders climb toward 2 as the step halves. The energy check X2 landed on 19 November 2026 (a part of its own). Rung 1's registered control, today's integrator with X2 on, then ran first, as the user chose (D232): its largest passing steps under the parity caps were 20 ms on the harness's calm stretch, held by charge stability, 1 ms through the cue, by the location rule, and 5 ms on a second world, by the junction-gate bound, and X2 refused nothing. By D232's rules a method was chosen on 20 November 2026 (D235): N2, the design note's linearly implicit step, as rung 1 as registered, then C, a fine-window executor, required and not optional. Rung 0's official verdict stays inconclusive (D232), and the fourth external review's fix makes its reader check each arm's identity, step and grid. Implemented and guarded: on main, with tests of the harness's judge and of the measurements M1, M2, M4 and M5, M1's on a registered world. M3, a measurement of cost, has no test of its own, and neither has rung 0's driver, which the engine's guard for restarts lists as a development tool.
